entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Charles de Bourbon, the oldest son of John I, Duke of Bourbon, and Marie, Duchess of Auvergne, played a crucial role in the late medieval period.

As the heir apparent to the Duchy of Bourbon, he was instrumental in shaping the region's politics and alliances during the 15th century.

His strategic marriages and military campaigns contributed significantly to the strengthening of the Bourbon dynasty, which would later become a dominant force in French history.

However, Charles' reign was also marked by power struggles with other noble families and the French monarchy, ultimately leading to his downfall.

The legacy of Charles de Bourbon can be seen in the continued influence of the Bourbon dynasty on French politics and society, even centuries after his death.

The most striking testament to his impact is the enduring Bourbon Restoration of 1815, which saw the restoration of the Bourbon monarchy and the reestablishment of the Bourbon dynasty as the ruling family of France.

This event serves as a poignant reminder of the lasting influence of Charles de Bourbon on the course of French history.

The Bourbon Restoration also highlights the complex and often tumultuous nature of the Bourbon dynasty's relationship with the French monarchy, a theme that continues to be explored by historians today.
